clue.text: Carriage behind, one in pursuit

parts.note: post- as a prefix means after or behind

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside that word

explanation.surface: A carriage trails behind, with one person giving chase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks positional, but the prefix post- means after; the one goes inside the pursuit word.
explanation.definitionFit: A post-chaise was a hired horse-drawn travelling coach, changed at posting stations.

clue.text: Toy with plectrum, a piece of tortoiseshell

parts.note: a guitar pick is a plectrum

indicators.note: just a piece of a word here means only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone fiddles with a tortoiseshell guitar plectrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toy' looks like a plaything noun, but 'Toy with' is a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick at food is to eat it half-heartedly, merely toying with it.

clue.text: It, left over time, harms ground in regularly flooded area

parts.note: it, as in sex appeal, is SA

indicators.note: ground up means crushed, so the letters are broken and reformed

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Something has been left too long and damages the ground in a flood-prone place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' meaning sex appeal (SA) is a crossword staple; in a down clue left sits over time.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt marsh is coastal land covered by the sea at high tides.

clue.text: E.g. one church dignitary, less sensitive

parts.note: a cardinal is a senior Catholic churchman

explanation.surface: A churchman is described as rather unfeeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' here is the comparative of numb, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: One is an example of a counting number such as one, two, three, used for quantity.

clue.text: Plug ceremonial clothing in speech

explanation.surface: Someone promotes formal attire during a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal talk delivered to an audience.

clue.text: Very good French composer produces curried meat on skewers

parts.note: so is an intensifier meaning very, as in so good

explanation.surface: An excellent French composer turns out a kebab dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good' only fills out the phrase; SO comes from the intensifier sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sosatie is a South African dish of curried marinated meat grilled on skewers.

clue.text: Help to eat cold tart

indicators.note: a word that eats another swallows it, holding it inside

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: An instruction to help someone eat a cold pastry tart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' looks like a pastry, but it is the adjective sour; AID swallows C to give ACID.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid things taste sharp and sour, which is the adjectival sense of tart.

clue.text: Dance clubs round northern Georgia

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs
N is the abbreviation for northern
GA is the postal code for the US state

explanation.surface: Nightclubs across the north of Georgia host a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin American line dance in which people follow one another.

clue.text: Revolutionary red spies spread about

indicators.note: a revolution overturns the order, so the letters are turned upside down

explanation.surface: Communist agents fan out across the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' fits the red spies so well it looks like an adjective, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To disperse is to scatter or go off in different directions.

clue.text: Let's get panther put out — act boldly

indicators.note: being put out means disturbed or upset, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A call to catch a big cat and throw it out, being brave about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp the nettle is an idiom meaning to tackle a difficulty firmly and courageously.

clue.text: Poor cards — losing badly in US resort

indicators.note: something done badly is messed up, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: the letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A card player holding a poor hand loses heavily at an American holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' reads as a description of the hand but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado Springs is a city and tourist destination at the foot of Pikes Peak in Colorado.

clue.text: Artist put back silk fabric in cupboard

indicators.note: putting something back here means setting it down from the end to the start

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: An artist returns some silk cloth to a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoire is a large wardrobe or tall cabinet, a French word for a free-standing cupboard.

clue.text: Series of questions tucked in with a will

parts.note: a test is a set of questions
to tuck in is to eat heartily

explanation.surface: Someone sits an exam and then tucks in to a meal with determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With a will' sounds like vigour, but here it is literal: having made a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies testate has left a valid legal will behind them.

clue.text: Coarse male in group in paper

indicators.note: one word in a group is placed inside the word for that group

explanation.surface: A vulgar man belongs to a crowd featured in a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The male goes inside the group word; the final 'in' joins wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsheet is a large-format newspaper, traditionally the serious kind.

clue.text: Cut-price lettuce?

indicators.note: a cut word is trimmed short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A shopper asks whether there is cheap lettuce on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut-price' reads as one word meaning cheap; split, it tells you to cut the price word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cos is a variety of lettuce with long crisp leaves, also called romaine.

clue.text: Charlie on straight and narrow?

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet
strict, as in a straight, rule-bound person

explanation.surface: Charlie is on the straight and narrow, living an honest life.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface splits the idiom 'straight and narrow'; 'narrow' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrict something is to squeeze it tighter, making it narrower.

clue.text: Mother with asthma perplexed sages

indicators.note: a perplexed thing is muddled and confused, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mother suffering asthma baffles wise men.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma is an Indian title for a revered wise person, as in Mahatma Gandhi.

clue.text: Timber when hard

parts.note: H is the pencil marking for hard

explanation.surface: Wood at the point when it has hardened.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a tree whose tough, pale wood is a common hardwood.

clue.text: Information about a loner lost in US city

indicators.note: one word about another goes round it
something lost has gone astray, so its letters wander out of order

parts.note: taken as written, as the fodder

explanation.surface: A report about a solitary person who has gone missing in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: New Orleans is the largest city in Louisiana, famous for jazz.

clue.text: We back cowboy film

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: We support a cowboy movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reads as a verb meaning support, but it is the noun for a ship's rear, not a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A western is a genre film set in the American Old West, typically featuring cowboys.

clue.text: After war is over conceal whip

indicators.note: a word that is over has been turned over, flipped end to end

explanation.surface: Once fighting ends, someone hides a whip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'War is over' sounds like peace, but it tells you to turn the word over.
explanation.definitionFit: A rawhide is a whip or rope made of untanned leather.

clue.text: A way of acting?

parts.note: surface reading: any manner of behaving
setter's reading: a school of stage performance, after Stanislavski, in which actors live the role

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that 'acting' is the theatre sense: the technique named after the system used by Brando and De Niro.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a way of doing anything, and is also the name of a famous immersive style of stage performance.

clue.text: Every so often volunteers wheeled by

indicators.note: something wheeled round turns about and faces the other way

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
in arithmetic, three by four is three times four

explanation.surface: Now and then volunteers are pushed past in wheelchairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' looks like 'past', but it is the multiplication sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at times happens occasionally, now and then.

clue.text: In boot or someone's trunk

indicators.note: the letters wanted sit in the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A body found in someone's car boot, the stuff of crime fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boot' and 'trunk' both suggest a car, but trunk is the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the body's trunk, without head or limbs.

clue.text: We, with remainder left inside, struggle

indicators.note: what lies inside sits between the letters of the outer word

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: We struggle, with the remaining people left inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the remainder and left go inside together, in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrestle is to grapple or fight with effort, a synonym of struggle.

clue.text: Actress in elite diner ordered with charm

indicators.note: something ordered has been arranged afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A film star at an exclusive restaurant orders with great charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene Dietrich was a German-born Hollywood film star and singer.

clue.text: Before you can say Jack Robinson and so on!

definitions.text: Before you can say Jack Robinson

explanation.surface: Something happens instantly, and so on, as the familiar list goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'and so on' supplies the letters directly once 'and' is read as a join.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Before you can say Jack Robinson' is an idiom for very quickly, which is what soon means.

clue.text: Dine with setter, unusually attentive

indicators.note: something done unusually departs from the normal order of things

explanation.surface: Eat out with the crossword compiler, who is remarkably attentive.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone interested is paying close attention, keen and engaged.
